authority: #K2-471 (the window authorised: implement the bounded via-escape branch, pin CANDS_MAX as a literal, close the regression fixture on every layer, RED->GREEN, re-run the precheck, GO => one N=1). Before paying for that implementation this record checks the window's PREMISE with a measurement - the same discipline that produced R1470 (a prescription was falsified before it was built) and R1512 (a ruling-named branch was missing). TWO findings, both decisive.

finding_1_the_via_branch_is_provably_SUB.statement: under the planner's own clearance model the via branch can NEVER turn a refusal into an escape, so landing it cannot change any precheck verdict - it would be dead code.
finding_1_the_via_branch_is_provably_SUB.model: _leg_clear uses need = clear + hw (0.30 + obstacle half-width). A via is a disc: _via_clear uses need = clear + via_r + hw (0.30 + 0.175 + hw). The via's requirement is STRICTLY LARGER than the leg's at the same point, and the via additionally needs its site reached (a clear in-plane prefix for r>0).
finding_1_the_via_branch_is_provably_SUB.proof_r0: if the in-plane ladder refuses, then in EVERY direction the k=1 leg (length 0.1) is blocked, i.e. in every direction there is an obstacle within (clear + hw) + 0.1 = 0.25 + hw of the pad centre. A via at the pad centre (r=0) needs a clear disc of clear + via_r + hw = 0.475 + hw. Since 0.25 + hw < 0.475 + hw, that same obstacle blocks the via. => r=0 can never rescue a refusal.
finding_1_the_via_branch_is_provably_SUB.proof_r_gt_0: for r >= step, the via candidate additionally requires a clear in-plane prefix [pad, v]; but the obstacle that blocks the k=1 leg in the SAME direction lies within 0.15+hw of the segment [pad, p_1] (length 0.1), which is a SUB-SEGMENT of that prefix, so the prefix is blocked and the candidate is skipped. => r>0 can never rescue a refusal either.
finding_1_the_via_branch_is_provably_SUB.empirical_confirmation: with the current (point) pad model the via-at-centre clearance to the nearest neighbour is 0.50mm while the via needs 0.625mm (0.30 + 0.175 + 0.15) => blocked, exactly as the proof says. The via branch was therefore NOT implemented this window: it is provably a no-op, and landing dead code would be false completeness.
finding_1_the_via_branch_is_provably_SUB.note: #K2-467 sec.2.1 does name the via branch; the gap R1512 found is real as a SPEC-vs-CODE gap, but the branch carries no decision power for this gate.

finding_2_the_two_refusals_are_artifacts.statement: the refusals are not a property of the board - they are produced by modelling every pad as a POINT with an ISOTROPIC half-width equal to max(size.x,size.y)/2. That is NOT the most permissive model: for a long thin pad it is ~5x too big.

point_model.half_width_used: max(0.300, 1.475)/2 = 0.7375 mm (an isotropic disc of radius 0.7375)
point_model.effect: a neighbour at 0.50mm pitch (GND @ (37.25,57.1625) and I2C2_SDA @ (38.25,57.1625) for pad 22) then needs clear + hw = 0.30 + 0.7375 = 1.0375mm of centre-to-centre room, so EVERY neighbour is fatal and every ray is blocked.

true_shape_model.shape: capsule along the pad's long axis: segment half-length (1.475-0.300)/2 = 0.5875, hw = 0.300/2 = 0.150
true_shape_model.why_the_escape_is_legal: along the LONG axis the same neighbour is 0.50mm away centre-to-centre and needs only clear + hw = 0.30 + 0.150 = 0.45mm => 0.50 >= 0.45 => the corridor is LEGAL (edge-to-edge 0.25mm vs the 0.20mm floor). This is exactly the geometry the R1440 witness uses: a short F.Cu run along the pad's long axis to a via at ~(37.75,56.2), i.e. 0.225mm beyond the pad's north tip.

decisive_read.method: read-only replay of plan_escapes() on the SAME board (/tmp/opencode/k2af/s1d_stitched.kicad_pcb), SAME obstacles (tracks exact), SAME criterion (clear=0.30, max_escape_len=2.0, step=0.1), changing ONLY the pad obstacle model.
decisive_read.target_set: the two UNCONNECTED ends only (#K2-468 sec.3.2): I2C2_SCL@U1.22 and I2C1_SDA@U1.48
decisive_read.conclusion: both ends own a deterministic in-plane escape along the pad's long axis; the refusal is a MODEL ARTIFACT.

corrects_two_recorded_claims: R1498: 'each PAD obstacle was modelled as a POINT with its half-size, which is SMALLER than the pad TRUE SHAPE, i.e. the MOST PERMISSIVE pad model' - FALSE for an anisotropic pad (0.30 x 1.475): the isotropic disc is 4.92x the true short half-axis.

#K2-468 sec.2: 'the refusals are conservative-real (a more faithful/larger obstacle can only REDUCE freedom)' - the model is not a lower bound on the pad; the true shape is SMALLER in the short direction and opens the long-axis corridor.

consequence.appendix_A: appendix A (sec.16.3 dead-exit / relocation) must NOT be used to relocate or redraw either pad: neither is a dead exit. Relocating U1 pad 22 would be exactly the 'wrongly relocated pad' risk #K2-470 was written to prevent.
consequence.do_not_run_n1: the gate reading under the current model is FALSE and the model is the thing under repair => no N=1 is taken.

proposed_fix_for_the_next_authorised_win: 1. the precheck must model each pad by its TRUE anisotropic shape (capsule / rounded rect along the long axis), not an isotropic disc.

2. the SOURCE pad's escape origin must leave the pad's own copper (or the asset must reach a free cell beyond the pad), so an asset is a USABLE corridor - a 0.1mm stub that still lies inside the pad is not an escape.
3. strengthen the asset criterion accordingly (require the corridor to reach a free cell / a usable length), because the current criterion 'any clear 0.1mm leg' is trivially satisfiable.
4. re-derive and PIN the bound literal as before, close the RED fixture on every reachable layer, and rerun the precheck (unconnected ends only).
5. only if that corrected gate is GO, take exactly one fresh N=1 (per #K2-468 sec.3.4 / #K2-470 sec.3.4).

capability_registration_proposed.root_cause: an accelerator/boundary model that is believed conservative but is not; an isotropic half-width on an anisotropic pad over-sizes the obstacle and manufactures refusals
capability_registration_proposed.remedy: model obstacles with their true shape; state, per model, whether it is an UPPER or LOWER bound on the real freedom, and do not claim 'permissive' without the geometry
capability_registration_proposed.closure_criterion: asset + same-class regression PASS (an anisotropic long pad enclosed short-axis, open long-axis => GO) + a corrected real-board precheck reading

evidence_reproducibility.note: read-only; two runs differ ONLY in how each pad is turned into an obstacle entry; both write nothing to the board

tried: plan_escapes() on the real board with the point+max-half pad model => go=False (2 named refusals)
plan_escapes() on the same board with the true anisotropic (capsule) pad model => go=True (0 refusals)
why_not_passing: the gate was refusing on its own model, not on the board
gap_layer: ENG precheck MODELLING layer (量具/模型层) - NOT the scheme/drawing layer, NOT the engine capability, NOT the criteria, NOT L1
not_done: the precheck rerun under a corrected model
